latin_incipit: Possibilis est prophetia in somnis per illustrationem intellectus agentis super animam nostram.
english_translation: Prophecy in dreams is possible through the illumination of our soul by the agent intellect.
charge: Averroes maintains that the agent intellect can impress intelligible forms onto the passive imagination during sleep.
defense: Pico accepts this doctrine as compatible with Christian theology, viewing such dreams as natural prophecy mediated by the divine intellect, not demonic deception.
exegesis: Averroes (influenced by Avicenna) viewed dreams as potential vehicles of prophecy when the agent intellect impresses forms onto the passive imagination. The intellectus agens acts as a divine transmitter of truth. This view stands close to Neoplatonism and supports the prophetic function of the philosopher-sage.

scholar_citations.work: Syncretism in the West: Pico's Platform

notes: Key to understanding Averroist epistemology and Pico's defense of natural prophecy against charges of magic.
